query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: achievement_gap
per_column.rationale: The gap between actual and target achievement is a measure of the OUTCOME (achievement) itself, not a constitutive practice/aspect of how goals are managed. It restates the success being explained rather than decomposing the management factors.

per_column.name: progress_status
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal is on_track/below/exceeds is the achievement outcome itself, a restatement of success, not a facet of the management practices that produce it.

per_column.name: priority_score
per_column.rationale: Prioritization is a genuine aspect OF goal-management practice; how goals are prioritized is a constitutive part of managing goals.

per_column.name: priority_completion_alignment
per_column.rationale: This correlates priority with completion, i.e., a derived relationship between a practice and an outcome. It is an analytic/predictive construct linking to achievement, not a standalone constitutive aspect of the management concept.

per_column.name: achievement_level
per_column.rationale: Achieved/in_progress/abandoned is the achievement outcome itself, a direct restatement of the success being studied, not a facet of the managing practices.

judge.rationale: The concept to decompose is the set of goal-MANAGEMENT PRACTICES that support achievement. A proper faceted decomposition would carve management practices into constitutive aspects such as goal setting/clarity, prioritization, ownership/accountability, cadence of tracking/updates, resourcing, and review/adjustment. Only priority_score is a true facet of the management practice. achievement_gap, progress_status, and achievement_level are all restatements of the achievement OUTCOME being explained, and they heavily overlap with each other (three encodings of the same outcome), badly harming mutual exclusivity. priority_completion_alignment is a derived practice-outcome correlation, an analytic/predictor construct rather than a constitutive facet. The set leaves the concept's main constitutive aspects (setting, tracking cadence, accountability, review) almost entirely uncovered, so exhaustiveness is very low.
